subject: Helix throughput runway & GPU scaling plan (renewal)
messages:
From: Aaron Lee <aaron@helixsys.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@helixsys.com
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Capacity planning for our renewal — Q3/Q4 runway

Hi Karthik / Marissa,

We’re starting to pull together internal numbers ahead of our Dec renewal and need a clear recommendation from Redwood on committed GPU counts and a short-term burst strategy. A few data points from our side:
- Current peak sustained traffic: ~95 QPS (average tokens per call ~620)
- Expected product-driven growth: ~3x by end of Q4 (peak ~285 QPS) with traffic spikes up to ~350 QPS for marketing events
- Hard requirement: predictable throughput for customer-facing routing, and <250ms token-latency target for median requests if possible

Can you share a sizing recommendation (reserved pool counts), a 12-month runway plan with step-ups, and an option that includes burst-on-demand for spikes? Also please include estimated committed pricing so I can run this by procurement. Attaching our internal Q2–Q4 forecast CSV.

Thanks,
Aaron
Head of Platform Engineering
Helix Systems

Attachment: helix_traffic_q2_q4.csv (CSV, 42KB)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Aaron Lee <aaron@helixsys.com>, Priya Desai <priya.desai@helixsys.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 13:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity planning for our renewal — Q3/Q4 runway

Aaron — thanks for the data. I ran the numbers with the attached capacity model and sketched three recommended scenarios (summary attached). Key assumptions up front: average request = 620 tokens, model variant = rwd-infer-3 (production profile we previously validated for Helix), and our throughput baseline per H100-equivalent GPU = ~28 sustained QPS at that payload (includes 15% headroom for batching/kv-cache).

Scenario A — Conservative (12-mo renewal, minimal step-up):
- Peak at renewal month: 120 QPS -> recommended reserved pool: 5 H100-eq GPUs
- Burst: +4 GPUs on-demand (pay-as-you-go)
- Notes: Covers current plus 20% buffer; modest cost uplift

Scenario B — Growth runway (12-mo renewal with step at month 6):
- Projected peak by Q4: 360 QPS -> base reserved pool: 13 H100-eq GPUs
- Add 3 spare GPUs for short-term bursts -> reserved commitment: 16 GPUs
- Autoscale / burst-on-demand: additional 8 GPUs available for marketing events
- SLA target: 95th pct tail under reserved + burst; median latency estimate ~180–230ms

Scenario C — Aggressive upsell (18-mo step commitments):
- Support peak 540 QPS -> reserved pool: 24 H100-eq GPUs + 8 burst
- For customers expecting large product launches

Costing: rough committed price per H100-eq GPU per month (list for negotiation) shown in spreadsheet; we can tighten numbers after you confirm the scenario.

Next steps: if you’re aligned with Scenario B we’ll draft a renewal addendum with step-up milestones and a requested signature path for procurement.

Files attached: helix_capacity_model_v1.xlsx, helix_capacity_scenarios_summary.pdf

—Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1-415-555-0192

Attachment: helix_capacity_model_v1.xlsx (XLSX, 1.2MB)
Attachment: helix_capacity_scenarios_summary.pdf (PDF, 320KB)

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 01 Jul 2026 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Helix throughput runway & GPU scaling plan (internal notes)

Quick internal notes on the model assumptions — leaving here for the record and for pricing negotiation:
- The ~28 QPS per H100-eq is conservative for rwd-infer-3 with 620 tokens avg. If Helix is willing to accept mixed precision + int8 quantization on non-sensitive routes, we can push to ~36 QPS/GPU (saves ~20–30% GPUs in Scenarios B/C).
- If they want stricter latency (median <150ms), we should assume smaller batch windows which reduces effective QPS per GPU to ~20. That drives Scenario B reserved pool to ~18 GPUs. We should present both latency-tuned and cost-tuned options.
- Recommend including a fall-back routing policy in the addendum: when reserved utilization >85% for >5min, spike traffic is routed to a lower-cost, compatible model variant or to on-demand cluster to protect tail latency. Adds operational safety without increasing committed count.

Also: Marissa, can you confirm whether procurement wants monthly billing or quarterly drawdown for committed pools? That will affect list price vs. committed discount structure.

—Priyom
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Jul 2026 09:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Helix throughput runway & GPU scaling plan (internal notes)

Agree with Priyom. A couple of commercial suggestions before we send a final to Helix:
- Offer a 12-month reserved commitment with an optional mid-term uplift at month 6 (pre-agreed increment of +20% GPUs) — this gives them runway while keeping our capacity commitments sane.
- Include a 90-day SLA exception credit if we cannot meet the 95th pct throughput during an agreed launch window (we cap to 1 event per 90 days).
- Present a quantization path as an optional service (engineering assist + validation) with a one-time implementation fee.

Evelyn — can you review SLA language and confirm we can commit to a 95th pct throughput SLO for reserved + 50% burst? If legal needs to tighten, we should capture in the addendum now.

—Marissa
Renewals Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Aaron Lee <aaron@helixsys.com>, Priya Desai <priya.desai@helixsys.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>, procurement@helixsys.com
Date: Wed, 07 Jul 2026 15:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Final sizing + options for Helix renewal — decision requested

Aaron / Priya — following internal review, attached is a concise one-pager and the workbook with the scenarios we discussed. TL;DR options below so procurement can pick a path quickly: 

Option 1 — Safe baseline (lowest cost, minimal uplift)
- Reserved: 5 H100-eq GPUs
- On-demand burst: +4 GPUs
- Recommended when Helix expects modest growth; median latency ~200ms

Option 2 — Growth runway (recommended for product-driven scale)
- Reserved: 16 H100-eq GPUs (13 capacity + 3 spares)
- Burst pool: +8 GPUs (on-demand)
- Step-up clause: commit to +20% at month 6 if average reserved utilization >65% over a 14-day window
- Estimated committed monthly cost: see spreadsheet (we can do a bundled discount for 12-month upfront)

Option 3 — High-velocity launches (aggressive)
- Reserved: 24 H100-eq GPUs + 8 burst

We recommend Option 2 for most predictable balance of cost vs. runway. If you want to pursue aggressive quantization before renewal to reduce GPUs, we can scope an engineering engagement (one-time).

Please confirm which option procurement prefers and whether a 12-month or 18-month term is acceptable. Once you pick, Marissa and I will generate the renewal addendum and send to procurement for signature.

Thanks — looking forward to your note.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com
